General information about Council meetings

Ordinary Meetings of Council are held once a month, except in January. Meetings commence at 3.30 pm.

Members of the public are able to address Council during the Public Forum about an item on the agenda or in relation to a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public. 

Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30 pm, subject to any registered speakers.

Public Forum and Meetings are live streamed (excluding closed sessions) in accordance withCouncil's Code of Meeting Practice. Members of the public attending or speaking at a meetingor Public Forumwill be recorded and publicly broadcast.

Contacting Councillors About Agenda Items

Members of the public who wish to make representations to Councillors regarding any item listed on the agenda for an upcoming Council meeting should contact Councillors directly by email. Councillor contact details are available on the Councillors page of this website. Councillors | Wingecarribee Shire Council

What to Expect:

The Council meets once a month except during the late December-Early January Summer break.

Community members are encouraged to come along and there is no need to register to do so.

If you would like the opportunity to speak on a matter from the Meeting Agenda you can register to speak at the Public Forum.

You may also register to address the Council about a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public.

Please note that by law, Council is required to livestream our meetings.  Anyone attending or speaking at the meeting will be included in the recording and public broadcast and if you have registered to speak.

Speak at Public Forum

Your opportunity to voice your input on any item from the Meeting Agenda.

You’ll need to register to speak at the Public Forum after the Meeting Agenda has been published on our website, and no later than 4:30pm two days prior to the Council Meeting you wish to address.

Legal representatives wishing to speak on behalf of others must make this known on their registration form.

Applicants are required to undertake that if approved to speak they will not make any defamatory comments or imputations, and that they agree to indemnify Council in respect of any defamatory statements or imputations they make.

Limited spots are available and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum.

If your application to speak is approved, five minutes will be allocated for you to make your presentation. You’ll be required to undertake that you will not make any defamatory comments or imputations and agree to indemnify Council in respect of any made in the course of your presentation. 

The Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30pm, subject to any registered speakers.

How can the public address the forum?

Members of the public can apply to address Council on any item that is on the agenda of Ordinary Council Meeting. A person may apply to speak on no more than one item of business on the agenda of the council meeting. 

A limited number of places are available to speak at each meeting.

All requests for consideration need to be submitted by 4:30 pm two business days prior to the meeting. This will generally be on the Monday in the week of the Council meeting using the Public Forum Application form.

To ensure an equal opportunity for members of the public to apply to speak, the form will only be accepted for consideration after the relevant Council meeting agenda is published on Council’s website.

Presentations by members of the public are limited to five minutes duration each and are restricted to two speakers 'for' and two speakers 'against' on an item of business. 

Legal representatives acting on behalf of others are not to be permitted to speak at a public forum unless they identify their status as a legal representative when applying to speak at the public forum.

The General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum. 

For further information about Public Forum see Council’s Code of Meeting Practice.

Speaking on a proposal to close a meeting to the public

Community members may make representations at a Council Meeting as to whether a part of the meeting should be closed, before the matter is dealt with.

If the matter has been identified in the Meeting Agenda as a matter that is likely to be considered once the meeting has closed to the public, you must first make an application to Council in order to make representation.

This application must be received by Council no later than 4.30pm, two business days prior to the meeting.

Two speakers will each be allocated one minute to make representations and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak.

General information about Council meetings

Ordinary Meetings of Council are held once a month, except in January. Meetings commence at 3.30 pm.

Members of the public are able to address Council during the Public Forum about an item on the agenda or in relation to a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public. 

Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30 pm, subject to any registered speakers.

Public Forum and Meetings are live streamed (excluding closed sessions) in accordance withCouncil's Code of Meeting Practice. Members of the public attending or speaking at a meetingor Public Forumwill be recorded and publicly broadcast.

Contacting Councillors About Agenda Items

Members of the public who wish to make representations to Councillors regarding any item listed on the agenda for an upcoming Council meeting should contact Councillors directly by email. Councillor contact details are available on the Councillors page of this website. Councillors | Wingecarribee Shire Council

What to Expect:

The Council meets once a month except during the late December-Early January Summer break.

Community members are encouraged to come along and there is no need to register to do so.

If you would like the opportunity to speak on a matter from the Meeting Agenda you can register to speak at the Public Forum.

You may also register to address the Council about a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public.

Please note that by law, Council is required to livestream our meetings.  Anyone attending or speaking at the meeting will be included in the recording and public broadcast and if you have registered to speak.

Speak at Public Forum

Your opportunity to voice your input on any item from the Meeting Agenda.

You’ll need to register to speak at the Public Forum after the Meeting Agenda has been published on our website, and no later than 4:30pm two days prior to the Council Meeting you wish to address.

Legal representatives wishing to speak on behalf of others must make this known on their registration form.

Applicants are required to undertake that if approved to speak they will not make any defamatory comments or imputations, and that they agree to indemnify Council in respect of any defamatory statements or imputations they make.

Limited spots are available and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum.

If your application to speak is approved, five minutes will be allocated for you to make your presentation. You’ll be required to undertake that you will not make any defamatory comments or imputations and agree to indemnify Council in respect of any made in the course of your presentation. 

The Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30pm, subject to any registered speakers.

How can the public address the forum?

Members of the public can apply to address Council on any item that is on the agenda of Ordinary Council Meeting. A person may apply to speak on no more than one item of business on the agenda of the council meeting. 

A limited number of places are available to speak at each meeting.

All requests for consideration need to be submitted by 4:30 pm two business days prior to the meeting. This will generally be on the Monday in the week of the Council meeting using the Public Forum Application form.

To ensure an equal opportunity for members of the public to apply to speak, the form will only be accepted for consideration after the relevant Council meeting agenda is published on Council’s website.

Presentations by members of the public are limited to five minutes duration each and are restricted to two speakers 'for' and two speakers 'against' on an item of business. 

Legal representatives acting on behalf of others are not to be permitted to speak at a public forum unless they identify their status as a legal representative when applying to speak at the public forum.

The General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum. 

For further information about Public Forum see Council’s Code of Meeting Practice.

Speaking on a proposal to close a meeting to the public

Community members may make representations at a Council Meeting as to whether a part of the meeting should be closed, before the matter is dealt with.

If the matter has been identified in the Meeting Agenda as a matter that is likely to be considered once the meeting has closed to the public, you must first make an application to Council in order to make representation.

This application must be received by Council no later than 4.30pm, two business days prior to the meeting.

Two speakers will each be allocated one minute to make representations and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak.

What to Expect:

The Council meets once a month except during the late December-Early January Summer break.

Community members are encouraged to come along and there is no need to register to do so.

If you would like the opportunity to speak on a matter from the Meeting Agenda you can register to speak at the Public Forum.

You may also register to address the Council about a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public.

Please note that by law, Council is required to livestream our meetings.  Anyone attending or speaking at the meeting will be included in the recording and public broadcast and if you have registered to speak.

Speak at Public Forum

Your opportunity to voice your input on any item from the Meeting Agenda.

You’ll need to register to speak at the Public Forum after the Meeting Agenda has been published on our website, and no later than 4:30pm two days prior to the Council Meeting you wish to address.

Legal representatives wishing to speak on behalf of others must make this known on their registration form.

Applicants are required to undertake that if approved to speak they will not make any defamatory comments or imputations, and that they agree to indemnify Council in respect of any defamatory statements or imputations they make.

Limited spots are available and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum.

If your application to speak is approved, five minutes will be allocated for you to make your presentation. You’ll be required to undertake that you will not make any defamatory comments or imputations and agree to indemnify Council in respect of any made in the course of your presentation. 

The Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30pm, subject to any registered speakers.

How can the public address the forum?

Members of the public can apply to address Council on any item that is on the agenda of Ordinary Council Meeting. A person may apply to speak on no more than one item of business on the agenda of the council meeting. 

A limited number of places are available to speak at each meeting.

All requests for consideration need to be submitted by 4:30 pm two business days prior to the meeting. This will generally be on the Monday in the week of the Council meeting using the Public Forum Application form.

To ensure an equal opportunity for members of the public to apply to speak, the form will only be accepted for consideration after the relevant Council meeting agenda is published on Council’s website.

Presentations by members of the public are limited to five minutes duration each and are restricted to two speakers 'for' and two speakers 'against' on an item of business. 

Legal representatives acting on behalf of others are not to be permitted to speak at a public forum unless they identify their status as a legal representative when applying to speak at the public forum.

The General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum. 

For further information about Public Forum see Council’s Code of Meeting Practice.

Speaking on a proposal to close a meeting to the public

Community members may make representations at a Council Meeting as to whether a part of the meeting should be closed, before the matter is dealt with.

If the matter has been identified in the Meeting Agenda as a matter that is likely to be considered once the meeting has closed to the public, you must first make an application to Council in order to make representation.

This application must be received by Council no later than 4.30pm, two business days prior to the meeting.

Two speakers will each be allocated one minute to make representations and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak.

General information about Council meetings

Ordinary Meetings of Council are held once a month, except in January. Meetings commence at 3.30 pm.

Members of the public are able to address Council during the Public Forum about an item on the agenda or in relation to a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public. 

Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30 pm, subject to any registered speakers.

Public Forum and Meetings are live streamed (excluding closed sessions) in accordance withCouncil's Code of Meeting Practice. Members of the public attending or speaking at a meetingor Public Forumwill be recorded and publicly broadcast.

Contacting Councillors About Agenda Items

Members of the public who wish to make representations to Councillors regarding any item listed on the agenda for an upcoming Council meeting should contact Councillors directly by email. What to Expect:

The Council meets once a month except during the late December-Early January Summer break.

Community members are encouraged to come along and there is no need to register to do so.

If you would like the opportunity to speak on a matter from the Meeting Agenda you can register to speak at the Public Forum.

You may also register to address the Council about a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public.

Please note that by law, Council is required to livestream our meetings.  Anyone attending or speaking at the meeting will be included in the recording and public broadcast and if you have registered to speak.

Speak at Public Forum

Your opportunity to voice your input on any item from the Meeting Agenda.

You’ll need to register to speak at the Public Forum after the Meeting Agenda has been published on our website, and no later than 4:30pm two days prior to the Council Meeting you wish to address.

Legal representatives wishing to speak on behalf of others must make this known on their registration form.

Applicants are required to undertake that if approved to speak they will not make any defamatory comments or imputations, and that they agree to indemnify Council in respect of any defamatory statements or imputations they make.

Limited spots are available and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum.

If your application to speak is approved, five minutes will be allocated for you to make your presentation. You’ll be required to undertake that you will not make any defamatory comments or imputations and agree to indemnify Council in respect of any made in the course of your presentation. 

The Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30pm, subject to any registered speakers.

How can the public address the forum?

Members of the public can apply to address Council on any item that is on the agenda of Ordinary Council Meeting. A person may apply to speak on no more than one item of business on the agenda of the council meeting. 

A limited number of places are available to speak at each meeting.

All requests for consideration need to be submitted by 4:30 pm two business days prior to the meeting. This will generally be on the Monday in the week of the Council meeting using the Public Forum Application form.

To ensure an equal opportunity for members of the public to apply to speak, the form will only be accepted for consideration after the relevant Council meeting agenda is published on Council’s website.

Presentations by members of the public are limited to five minutes duration each and are restricted to two speakers 'for' and two speakers 'against' on an item of business. 

Legal representatives acting on behalf of others are not to be permitted to speak at a public forum unless they identify their status as a legal representative when applying to speak at the public forum.

The General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum. 

For further information about Public Forum see Council’s Code of Meeting Practice.

Speaking on a proposal to close a meeting to the public

Community members may make representations at a Council Meeting as to whether a part of the meeting should be closed, before the matter is dealt with.

If the matter has been identified in the Meeting Agenda as a matter that is likely to be considered once the meeting has closed to the public, you must first make an application to Council in order to make representation.

This application must be received by Council no later than 4.30pm, two business days prior to the meeting.

Two speakers will each be allocated one minute to make representations and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak.

General information about Council meetings

Ordinary Meetings of Council are held once a month, except in January. Meetings commence at 3.30 pm.

Members of the public are able to address Council during the Public Forum about an item on the agenda or in relation to a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public. 

Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30 pm, subject to any registered speakers.

Public Forum and Meetings are live streamed (excluding closed sessions) in accordance withCouncil's Code of Meeting Practice. Members of the public attending or speaking at a meetingor Public Forumwill be recorded and publicly broadcast.

Contacting Councillors About Agenda Items

Members of the public who wish to make representations to Councillors regarding any item listed on the agenda for an upcoming Council meeting should contact Councillors directly by email. What to Expect:

The Council meets once a month except during the late December-Early January Summer break.

Community members are encouraged to come along and there is no need to register to do so.

If you would like the opportunity to speak on a matter from the Meeting Agenda you can register to speak at the Public Forum.

You may also register to address the Council about a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public.

Please note that by law, Council is required to livestream our meetings.  Anyone attending or speaking at the meeting will be included in the recording and public broadcast and if you have registered to speak.

Speak at Public Forum

Your opportunity to voice your input on any item from the Meeting Agenda.

You’ll need to register to speak at the Public Forum after the Meeting Agenda has been published on our website, and no later than 4:30pm two days prior to the Council Meeting you wish to address.

Legal representatives wishing to speak on behalf of others must make this known on their registration form.

Applicants are required to undertake that if approved to speak they will not make any defamatory comments or imputations, and that they agree to indemnify Council in respect of any defamatory statements or imputations they make.

Limited spots are available and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum.

If your application to speak is approved, five minutes will be allocated for you to make your presentation. You’ll be required to undertake that you will not make any defamatory comments or imputations and agree to indemnify Council in respect of any made in the course of your presentation. 

The Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30pm, subject to any registered speakers.

How can the public address the forum?

Members of the public can apply to address Council on any item that is on the agenda of Ordinary Council Meeting. A person may apply to speak on no more than one item of business on the agenda of the council meeting. 

A limited number of places are available to speak at each meeting.

All requests for consideration need to be submitted by 4:30 pm two business days prior to the meeting. This will generally be on the Monday in the week of the Council meeting using the Public Forum Application form.

To ensure an equal opportunity for members of the public to apply to speak, the form will only be accepted for consideration after the relevant Council meeting agenda is published on Council’s website.

Presentations by members of the public are limited to five minutes duration each and are restricted to two speakers 'for' and two speakers 'against' on an item of business. 

Legal representatives acting on behalf of others are not to be permitted to speak at a public forum unless they identify their status as a legal representative when applying to speak at the public forum.

The General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum. 

For further information about Public Forum see Council’s Code of Meeting Practice.

Speaking on a proposal to close a meeting to the public

Community members may make representations at a Council Meeting as to whether a part of the meeting should be closed, before the matter is dealt with.

If the matter has been identified in the Meeting Agenda as a matter that is likely to be considered once the meeting has closed to the public, you must first make an application to Council in order to make representation.

This application must be received by Council no later than 4.30pm, two business days prior to the meeting.

Two speakers will each be allocated one minute to make representations and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak.

What to Expect:

The Council meets once a month except during the late December-Early January Summer break.

Community members are encouraged to come along and there is no need to register to do so.

If you would like the opportunity to speak on a matter from the Meeting Agenda you can register to speak at the Public Forum.

You may also register to address the Council about a proposal to close part of a meeting to the public.

Please note that by law, Council is required to livestream our meetings.  Anyone attending or speaking at the meeting will be included in the recording and public broadcast and if you have registered to speak.

Speak at Public Forum

Your opportunity to voice your input on any item from the Meeting Agenda.

You’ll need to register to speak at the Public Forum after the Meeting Agenda has been published on our website, and no later than 4:30pm two days prior to the Council Meeting you wish to address.

Legal representatives wishing to speak on behalf of others must make this known on their registration form.

Applicants are required to undertake that if approved to speak they will not make any defamatory comments or imputations, and that they agree to indemnify Council in respect of any defamatory statements or imputations they make.

Limited spots are available and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum.

If your application to speak is approved, five minutes will be allocated for you to make your presentation. You’ll be required to undertake that you will not make any defamatory comments or imputations and agree to indemnify Council in respect of any made in the course of your presentation. 

The Public Forum will take place prior to a Council Meeting, commencing at 2.30pm, subject to any registered speakers.

How can the public address the forum?

Members of the public can apply to address Council on any item that is on the agenda of Ordinary Council Meeting. A person may apply to speak on no more than one item of business on the agenda of the council meeting. 

A limited number of places are available to speak at each meeting.

All requests for consideration need to be submitted by 4:30 pm two business days prior to the meeting. This will generally be on the Monday in the week of the Council meeting using the Public Forum Application form.

To ensure an equal opportunity for members of the public to apply to speak, the form will only be accepted for consideration after the relevant Council meeting agenda is published on Council’s website.

Presentations by members of the public are limited to five minutes duration each and are restricted to two speakers 'for' and two speakers 'against' on an item of business. 

Legal representatives acting on behalf of others are not to be permitted to speak at a public forum unless they identify their status as a legal representative when applying to speak at the public forum.

The General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum. 

For further information about Public Forum see Council’s Code of Meeting Practice.

Speaking on a proposal to close a meeting to the public

Community members may make representations at a Council Meeting as to whether a part of the meeting should be closed, before the matter is dealt with.

If the matter has been identified in the Meeting Agenda as a matter that is likely to be considered once the meeting has closed to the public, you must first make an application to Council in order to make representation.

This application must be received by Council no later than 4.30pm, two business days prior to the meeting.

Two speakers will each be allocated one minute to make representations and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak.

Members of the public can apply to address Council on any item that is on the agenda of Ordinary Council Meeting. A person may apply to speak on no more than one item of business on the agenda of the council meeting. 

A limited number of places are available to speak at each meeting.

All requests for consideration need to be submitted by 4:30 pm two business days prior to the meeting. This will generally be on the Monday in the week of the Council meeting using the Public Forum Application form.

To ensure an equal opportunity for members of the public to apply to speak, the form will only be accepted for consideration after the relevant Council meeting agenda is published on Council’s website.

Presentations by members of the public are limited to five minutes duration each and are restricted to two speakers 'for' and two speakers 'against' on an item of business. 

Legal representatives acting on behalf of others are not to be permitted to speak at a public forum unless they identify their status as a legal representative when applying to speak at the public forum.

The General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak at the Public Forum. 

For further information about Public Forum see Council’s Code of Meeting Practice.

Speaking on a proposal to close a meeting to the public

Community members may make representations at a Council Meeting as to whether a part of the meeting should be closed, before the matter is dealt with.

If the matter has been identified in the Meeting Agenda as a matter that is likely to be considered once the meeting has closed to the public, you must first make an application to Council in order to make representation.

This application must be received by Council no later than 4.30pm, two business days prior to the meeting.

Two speakers will each be allocated one minute to make representations and the General Manager or their delegate may refuse an application to speak. 

Council Resolution Register

A Council resolution is a formal decision made during a Council meeting, guiding actions, policies, and initiatives. Recorded in the meeting minutes, resolutions shape Council’s work for the community. Use the Resolutions Register to search for decisions from September 2014 to the present.
